 Supplement Recall: Popular Product Receives FDA’s Highest Risk Warning
 Amelia NF/Getty Images 
 By 
 Alex Vance 
 Published on Nov. 19, 2026
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 The update comes nearly three weeks after the herbal supplement was pulled from shelves nationwide. Here's what to know.
 There are plenty of ways to help manage stress , from meditation and exercise to spending time outdoors or taking medication. But some people prefer a more natural approach, turning to herbal supplements like ashwagandha.
 Ashwagandha is an evergreen shrub grown in India and regions of Nepal that’s commonly marketed as a means of helping reduce stress, promote relaxation, and improve sleep . However, one brand is under recall due to potential Salmonella contamination—and now the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has assigned it its highest risk classification due to “Possible Salmonella contamination.”
 On November 12, the FDA classified a recall of 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules as Class I, nearly three weeks after it was initiated. It’s the agency’s most serious risk level , meaning there is “a reasonable probability” that using or being exposed to the product could cause serious health consequences or death.
 Recall background
 Vitality Works Inc. of Albuquerque, New Mexico, first announced the recall on October 30 after routine sampling identified potential Salmonella contamination. The recall affects 10,176 bottles of 120-count 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules, which were available nationwide online through Amazon.com and at Whole Foods Market stores from November 24, 2025, through October 20, 2026.
 According to product photos included in the initial company announcement, the capsules are packaged in a white bottle displaying a blue label.
 The FDA report lists the following details:
 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules, 120-count 
 Product Item Number: 3006661
 UPC: 099482520991 
 Lot number: 202526227
 Expiration date: 10-13-28
 As of the October 30 company announcement, no illnesses had been reported. Consumers should not use the recalled supplement and should discard it rather than return it to the store. Refunds are available at any Whole Foods Market location.
 Partly because the FDA does not approve dietary supplements for safety and effectiveness before they are made available to the public, the agency suggests talking with “a health care professional—such as your doctor, nurse, registered dietician, or pharmacist—about the benefits and risks” before starting any supplements.
